title: Going Retro to make up the difference
author: leather-armor
selftext:
Like many people opposed to AI will point out, no triple-A-quality games are being pushed out by AI-focused teams. Fair enough. But it's absolutely bonkers that I, alone, with a software engineering background and a vision, pushed out something that feels like what Data East would take 6 months to finish.  
  
I feel like going retro lets us produce higher-quality work while still making it valuable, rather than trying to push out a contemporary GTA clone and falling short by a significant margin. Basically, I appreciate that the entry barrier is definitely lower now, but if you're trying to code up BG3 by yourself, you'll soon see that the barrier there is definitely still pretty high, but if you want to make something similar to Megaman 7, in your vision, and with different level mechanics you always dreamed of... that is pretty achievable solo right now, I feel.  
  
What do y'all think? AM I overselling the capacities we get with AI to go solo + retro? Underselling how close we are to everyone coding up their own GTA 6?  
  
I'm already looking forward to my next game, with a focus on dialogue that I myself get to write, dream up, and voice with AI, which can even use my voice as input. I get to do the fun writing stuff while AI gets to create the art for Steam achievements that I don't care that much about.  
  
I feel like managing our ambitions is what will empower us the most, at least those of us who are truly solo. Having more of a team will certainly get you much farther, but I can't really speak on that experience.

comments.author: JorgitoEstrella
comments.body: How long did it take you to make this game?

replies.author: leather-armor
replies.body: From what I can see from git logs, first batch of work was commited Apr 12th, and the video reflects a build from May 5th, I believe.

replies.author: leather-armor
replies.body: I'm hoping I'll have it finished to my satisfaction before June.

comments.author: PSloVR
comments.body: I totally agree, I've been amazed at how far I can get a fun little top down shooter working that actually looks and plays well.  Something I would never have time to make before.  I think we'll see some really amazing solo projects in the near future.

comments.author: intelligent_rat
comments.body:
> if you want to make something similar to Megaman 7, in your vision, and with different level mechanics you always dreamed of... that is pretty achievable solo right now, I feel.

This has been achievable without AI as a solo developer for a long time. Reminder that Roller Coaster Tycoon was developed entirely solo by one guy in 1999, long before the advent of AI development tools.
